english.title: Disclose private sexual photographs and films with intent to cause distress
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) disclosed a private sexual photograph or film without the consent of **(..SPECIFY NAME OF INDIVIDUAL..), an individual who appeared in the photograph or film, with the intention of causing that individual distress
english.legislation: Contrary to section 33(1) and (9) of the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
disclosed a private sexual photograph / film
w/o consent of an individual who appeared in the photograph / film
with the intention of causing that individual distress

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence relates to 'disclose a private sexual photograph' only and is to be used for offences committed before the 29th June 2021. For offences committed on or after 29th June, see offence H22840 which includes 'to disclose' and 'threats to disclose'.
(ii) The offence is not committed if the disclosure of the photograph or film is made to the individual who appears in the photo/film
(iii) A person charged with an offence under this section is not to be taken to have disclosed a photograph or film with the intention of causing distress merely because that was a natural and probable consequence of the disclosure
(iv) Various defences are outlined in section 33(3) - (6)
(v) Schedule 8 to the Act makes special provision in connection with the operation of section 33 in relation to persons providing information society services.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.

Time Limit For Prosecutions:
None
